summary: Screw-pile light on a Matagorda Bay shoal, lit 1858 and sold 1942: a 1934 keeper's disappearance, 1913-1925 rescues, and a move ashore to Port Lavaca.

lens.where: The US Lighthouse Society lists the current optic as removed.

structures.note: Hexagonal wooden house on seven iron screw piles, each 25 feet long; the USLHS record gives 35 feet above mean high water.

access.note: The US Lighthouse Society's record lists it as open to the public. LighthouseFriends says it still welcomes visitors to Port Lavaca.

facts.agency: Calhoun County Historical Society (owner per LighthouseFriends visitor information); the 1978 gift went to the Calhoun County Historical Commission (Texas Maritime Museum). The sources do not reconcile the two names.

events.note: Hexagonal screw-pile house completed by 1 July 1858.
Fixed white light, sixth-order Fresnel lens.
USLHS gives 1858 for the original lens: lens lantern, then sixth-order, then fourth-order Fresnel.
DISPUTED: the 1937 Lighthouse Service Bulletin sketch says a light on Halfmoon Reef was completed by 1850. Every other source here gives 1858.

Light put out during the Civil War (1861-1865); no source gives the year it went out. The marker says Confederate troops disabled it; LighthouseFriends says it was extinguished but not dismantled or damaged.
Returned to service 20 February 1868.
1875 hurricane devastated Indianola and destroyed the East Shoal and West Shoal lights; LighthouseFriends says Halfmoon Reef suffered little damage.
Hurricane damage was moderate; the Lighthouse Board discontinued the light rather than repair it and kept the house as a daymark.
Fourth-order red lens in service 15 September 1902.
Steeper roof added to stop persistent leaks.
16 September: keeper Charles W. Heartt towed the disabled launch Nettie to port and gave her crew food.
18 August 1916 hurricane damaged Lighthouse Service property at Half Moon Reef and four other stations.
6 January: keeper George W. Anderson assisted the captain of the launch Oma B., stranded near the station in a gale.
Hurricane of 13-14 September 1919 severely damaged the light; assistant keeper A. E. Fox commended for maintaining it. LighthouseFriends says Fox was trapped on the station.
Fiscal 1922: keeper G. W. Anderson went to help fishermen adrift in an open boat two miles from shore. The report gives no day.
1 February: keeper Charles M. Teller towed the sailboat Herbert D to Palacios.
17 April: assistant keeper W. A. Madden helped the motor boat Marine, aground on the reef, and piloted her to Palacios.
Keeper H. O. Welch last seen 13 December 1934 when boatmen took him to the light; the light found dark three days later; body found 28 December. Accounts differ on where the body was found.
Assistant keeper post eliminated; eight-day lantern installed so the keeper could live ashore.
A hurricane tore the walkway from the lighthouse and left it sagging on its pilings.
USLHS record: discontinued 1942.
Moved to Point Comfort, about seven miles away, by barge.
Bill Bauer donated the lighthouse to the Calhoun County Historical Commission for use as a museum, with a trust fund for upkeep.
Restored as an Eagle Scout service project after the house was moved across the Matagorda Causeway.
Texas Historical Commission marker 2332 (its inscription says erected 1980). LighthouseFriends dates the marker's unveiling to 1985.
Placed on its present piers at Port Lavaca with a porch and three flagpoles (LighthouseFriends). The marker's own text says 'relocated here in 1979'.

notes_for_editor: PLACE/NAME: LighthouseFriends, the marker and the USLHS record name it Halfmoon Reef; the 1934 AP copy says Half Moon reef. SAME NAME, DIFFERENT PLACE: the Lighthouse Board reports for 1891-1901 (lhb corpus) list a 'Half moon Shoal' light in Galveston Bay. Those entries are a different light and are NOT used. DATE CONFLICT: the 1937 Lighthouse Service Bulletin sketch (PDF p. 50) says a lighthouse on Halfmoon Reef was completed by 1850; the USLHS record, LighthouseFriends and the marker give 1858. The page image was checked at 300 dpi and reads 'a lighthouse on Halfmoon Reef was completed by 1850. Other lights at Bolivar Point and Matagorda were in service by 1852', so the year is confirmed as printed; the story reports it as the Bulletin's claim. NOT FOUND: Lighthouse Board annual reports 1858-1890 are not in the local corpus, so the 1854 petition, the 1858 completion, the 1868 relight, the 1875 and 1886 decisions, and the Civil War wording rest on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted site, facts only) and the USLHS record. Wikipedia was read for leads only: its Civil War purpose (blockade runners) is not used from Wikipedia; the marker supports it, and the story cites the marker. Its 20-foot height is not used. MARKER DATE: the marker inscription says 'Erected 1980' and its text says the house was 'relocated here in 1979'; LighthouseFriends dates the marker's unveiling to 1985. The story states both. BODY LOCATION: the AP (Brownsville Herald, 29 Dec 1934) says Pass Cavallo, three miles away; LighthouseFriends says near Port O'Connor, twelve miles away. Both are in the story. WELCH WEEKDAY: the AP (San Antonio Light, 27 Dec 1934) says 'Friday, December 13'; 13 December 1934 was a Thursday. The story gives the date without a weekday. WELCH ROLE: the roster lists him as first assistant 1930-1934; the 1934 AP calls him the keeper. OCR MATCHES: (a) the 1919 commendation (PDF p. 41) prints the station as 'Hu1fmoon Heef' and the name as 'assi:tallt'; read from context and corroborated by the 1918-1923 Bulletin index entry 'Fox, A.E., asst keeper Halfmoon Reef, commended'. The page image was not separately viewed. (b) The 1913 entry gives 'September 16' without a year; 1913 is taken from the volume (PDF p. 38, checked in the text). (c) Commissioner fiscal 1921 scan p. 656 has a printed page marked '?' and is cited by scan page. The Commissioner fiscal-year boundaries were checked: the 1920 work-in-progress entry (scan 547) falls in the report for the year ended 30 June 1920 (line range of the volume), the 1921 entry (scan 656) in the year ended 30 June 1921, and the fishermen entry (scan 755) in the year ended 30 June 1922. OWNERSHIP TODAY: LighthouseFriends' visitor information says the Calhoun County Historical Society owns the lighthouse; the 1978 gift went to the Calhoun County Historical Commission. The story says the names are not reconciled. ATMOSPHERE: removed an editorial 'The bay needed lights of its own' and rewrote the Welch details to the AP's words. PRIVACY: Bill Bauer and Henry Smith are named only in their public roles as the sources print them (the 1942-1978 owners). A keeper's son born at the station in 1914, a later resident of the house and the Eagle Scout who restored it are not named. PHOTOS: the station record's Wikimedia Commons image was not checked for licence and is not added here. Roster line count: 45 stints, per roster.py; person slugs match roster.py --json.
